title: Word class and word family
summary: Identify the noun, verb, adjective or adverb slot in a sentence, then use word-family form, meaning and collocation to eliminate impossible options.

sections.title: Name the job before choosing the word
content: Compare: ‘The team decided quickly’, ‘The decision was quick’, ‘It was a decisive vote’ and ‘They voted decisively’. The shared idea stays related, but decide, decision, decisive and decisively perform different grammatical jobs.
Cover the options and label the empty slot first: noun, verb, adjective or adverb. This turns a vague vocabulary guess into a testable sentence decision.

sections.title: Read the sentence frame around the slot
content: A determiner or possessive often opens a noun slot: ‘the decision’, ‘her accuracy’. A modal such as must or can takes the base form of a verb: ‘must verify’. A linking verb such as be, seem or become often connects the subject to an adjective: ‘the route is accessible’. An adverb can modify how an action happens: ‘explained clearly’.

These frames are evidence, not automatic answers. Some words can belong to more than one class, not every adverb ends in -ly, and a grammatically possible form can still have the wrong meaning or collocation. Use the order slot, form, meaning, sentence.

sections.title: Use one family without confusing its members
content: In ‘After reviewing the trial, the committee reached a final ___’, the article a and adjective final prepare a noun. Decision fits that slot. Decide is a verb, decisive is an adjective and decisively is an adverb, so those forms fail before their general meaning needs closer comparison.

Now restore the whole sentence: ‘reached a final decision about whether to continue it’ is both grammatical and meaningful. Stopping after a suffix guess is unsafe; the complete sentence is the final check.

sections.title: Label the slot and explain each elimination
content: For two items, name the sentence signal, the required class and the reason every other family member fails. Do not choose merely because a form looks familiar.

sections.title: Apply slot, form, meaning, sentence
content: On three unseen items, predict the word class before viewing the options. Select a family member only after it fits the frame, keeps the intended meaning and sounds natural in the complete sentence.

sections.title: Locate the failed decision
content: Use four error labels. Slot error: the surrounding frame was misread. Family confusion: the right root but wrong class was selected. Form error: the class was right but tense, number or base form was wrong. Meaning or collocation mismatch: the grammar worked but the complete sentence did not.

Record the earliest failed step and one repair. If the slot was missed, underline its signals. If two forms are grammatical, compare meaning and natural combination rather than inventing a universal suffix rule.

sections.title: Transfer the family decision
content: Complete one unseen word-family item without a class label. An error enters the retry queue with a fresh parallel item rather than repeating the exposed sentence.
